items.stem: A task only needs to read source files. What permission posture fits?

options.text: Grant read access and withhold write, execute and network it does not need
options.rationale: Correct: least-privilege grants only what the task requires.

options.text: Grant full read, write, execute and network to avoid prompts
options.rationale: Over-granting expands the blast radius unnecessarily.

options.text: Grant write access in case it is needed later
Disable all permissions so it can do nothing
options.rationale: Blocking the needed read prevents the task entirely.

items.explanation: Correct: least-privilege grants only what the task requires.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO protect secrets when working with Claude Code? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keep API keys in a secret manager or environment, not in prompts
options.rationale: Correct: secrets belong outside prompts and context files.

options.text: Prevent secrets from appearing in command output and logs
options.rationale: Correct: leaked output is a common exfiltration path.

options.text: Paste the production key into CLAUDE.md for convenience
options.rationale: Context files must never contain secrets.

options.text: Echo the key to confirm it is correct
options.rationale: Echoing a secret leaks it into logs and history.

items.explanation: Correct: secrets belong outside prompts and context files.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A single narrow step needs one extra permission. The right approach is to:

options.text: Grant the minimum scoped permission for that step, not a broad one
options.rationale: Correct: scope the grant to the narrow action actually required.

options.text: Grant full permissions to avoid future prompts
options.rationale: Broad grants to unblock one step violate least-privilege.
A scoped grant lets the task proceed safely.

options.text: Disable the permission model for the session
options.rationale: Turning off controls removes all protection.

items.explanation: Correct: scope the grant to the narrow action actually required.
